subtitle: Midterm Important MCQs
topics: Dealing with Legacy Systems: Solutions, Wrapping & Migration

mcqs.question: According to the Law of Continuing Change (Lehman and Belady), a program that is used in a real-world environment must:
options: Be frozen once it is delivered
Change, or become progressively less useful in that environment
Be rewritten from scratch every year
Be outsourced to a specialist organization

mcqs.question: The Law of Increasing Complexity states that as a program evolves:
options: It becomes less complex with every release
It becomes more complex, and extra resources are needed to preserve and simplify its structure

mcqs.question: The well-known laws of software evolution were proposed by:
In its simplest form, software re-engineering means:
options: Re-organising and modifying existing software systems to make them more maintainable
Testing software before it is delivered
Developing a new system without studying the old one
Translating user manuals into another language

mcqs.question: "The examination of a subject system to re-constitute it in a new form and the subsequent implementation of the new form" is the definition of:

options: Cost, schedule, or risk to the customer

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a goal of software re-engineering?
options: To stop all future maintenance of the system
To increase the complexity of the existing system
To discard all artifacts of the existing system
To understand the artifacts of the existing system, namely specification, design, implementation and documentation

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a risk involved in re-engineering?
options: The existing system becomes too well documented
The target system may not have the same functionality as the existing system
The system becomes too easy to change

mcqs.question: Software systems are re-engineered keeping general objectives in mind. Which of the following is NOT one of those objectives?
options: Increasing the size of the development team

mcqs.question: Which situation most clearly indicates that a system needs re-engineering?
options: The users are fully satisfied with the system
The code follows all coding standards
The original developers have departed and the documentation is obsolete

mcqs.question: A major motivation for re-engineering is that, compared to re-development, re-engineering involves:
options: Complete replacement of the system at once
No understanding of the existing system

mcqs.question: Unlike hardware, software does not:
Software evolution means:
options: A continual change from a lesser, simpler, or worse state to a higher or better state
Keeping an installed system running with no change to its design
Preventing software from failing by means of bug fixing
Replacing worn-out parts of a system

mcqs.question: In the evolution-versus-maintenance distinction, maintenance means:
options: Adding major new features to the system
Changing the system to a higher or better state
Preventing software from failing to deliver its intended functionalities by means of bug fixing
Replacing the whole system at once

options: Software physically wears out like hardware
New requirements emerge when the software is used

mcqs.question: The driver for system evolution is:
options: The age of the programming language

mcqs.question: The software evolution process depends on:
options: The type of software being maintained, the development processes used, and the skills and experience of the people involved
The marketing strategy of the organization

options: Making major changes to the architecture of the system
Fixing bugs and improving the design so that future changes are less expensive
Developing a new system from scratch

mcqs.question: Software maintenance does NOT involve:
options: Making major changes to the architecture of the system

mcqs.question: In hardware (physical system) maintenance, a system or component is:
options: Returned to its original good state, often by replacing broken and worn-out parts

mcqs.question: A study on estimating software maintenance found that the cost of maintenance is as high as ______ of the cost of the entire software process cycle.
Corrective maintenance includes modifications and updations done in order to:
options: Keep the software tuned to the changing technology
Correct or fix problems discovered by users or concluded from user error reports
Add new features requested by users
Prevent future problems of the software

mcqs.question: Adaptive maintenance is performed to:
options: Keep the software product up-to-date and tuned to the ever-changing world of technology and business environment
Fix problems reported in error reports
Improve the internal structure to avoid future faults

mcqs.question: Perfective maintenance includes modifications done to:
options: Prevent problems that are not significant at the moment
Keep the software usable over a long period, including new features and new user requirements to improve reliability and performance
Adapt the software to a new operating system

mcqs.question: Preventive maintenance aims to:
options: Port the software to a new platform
Add new features to the software
Attend to problems which are not significant at this moment but may cause serious issues in the future

options: Greater than development costs, from 2 to 100 times depending on the application

mcqs.question: Maintenance costs are affected by:
options: Only the age of the hardware

mcqs.question: Regarding the team stability factor, maintenance costs are reduced if:
options: The same staff are involved with the system for some time
The developers have no responsibility for the system
The maintenance team is changed frequently

mcqs.question: The contractual responsibility factor increases maintenance cost because:
options: The system is too well documented

mcqs.question: According to the staff skills factor, maintenance staff are often:
options: The original developers of the system
Inexperienced and have limited domain knowledge
The most experienced staff with full domain knowledge

mcqs.question: According to the program age and structure factor, as programs age:
options: Their structure is degraded and they become harder to understand and change

mcqs.question: Maintenance prediction is concerned with:
options: Counting the number of developers needed
Estimating the marketing cost of the software
Predicting the delivery date of a new system
Assessing which parts of the system may cause problems and have high maintenance costs

mcqs.question: Predicting the number of changes requires an understanding of the relationship between a system and its environment. Which of the following influences this relationship?
options: The number and complexity of system interfaces
The office location of the maintenance team
The color scheme of the user interface

mcqs.question: Predictions of maintainability can be made by assessing the complexity of system components. This complexity depends on:
options: The number of users of the system

mcqs.question: Maintenance prediction complexity also depends on:
options: The number of computers in the organization
The version of the operating system

mcqs.question: Tightly coupled systems are a maintenance concern because they:
options: Require changes whenever the environment is changed

mcqs.question: A legacy system is a piece of software that:

mcqs.question: A legacy system can neither be replaced nor upgraded except at:

mcqs.question: The four characteristics of a legacy project are:

options: More code means more existing bugs and a higher probability of a new change causing a regression

Large projects are always replaced quickly

mcqs.question: Legacy code is often characterized as:
options: Untestable or untested, inflexible, and encumbered by technical debt

mcqs.question: Technical debt is:
options: The money borrowed to buy hardware
The coding you must do tomorrow because you took a shortcut in order to deliver the software today

options: Without addition or reduction of features in the transformed target source code

options: Re-engineers only a part of the system
Re-engineers a few procedures at a time
